results.title: Like-for-Like Quotes on Managed B200, B300, and NVL72 Capacity
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
Our managed clusters list H200 and B200 node types today.

...

## How GMI Cloud answers the RFQ

Managed GPU Cluster provides fully managed, Kubernetes-based multi-node GPU clusters for distributed training and large-scale inference, with centralized cluster lifecycle management. It's in early access. Managed clusters list H200 and B200 node types, with B200 in pre-order like the rest of our Blackwell lineup. GMI provisions and operates these clusters inside GMI-operated data centers, with deployment across the US, APAC, and EU.

For the Blackwell rows of the RFQ:

- HGX B200. B200 is pre-order, and the GPU page lists pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour. B200 is one of the listed node types for managed clusters.
- NVL72. GB200 NVL72 is pre-order, and the GPU pricing page lists pricing from $8.00 per GPU-hour. GB300 NVL72 is also pre-order, with pricing through our sales team. NVL72 is not among the published managed-cluster node types, so ask whether the managed layer is included, which layers it covers, and the billing unit behind the rate, and get all three in writing.
- B300. B300 is a hardware option on Prime Inference, our dedicated single-tenant inference service, where it's listed with 288 GB of HBM3e per GPU, and like the rest of our Blackwell lineup it is in pre-order. Prime bills per GPU-hour, with reserved capacity available seasonally or annually at lower hourly rates. That makes it a fair comparison for B300 inference capacity but not for a managed B300 training cluster, which should be quoted by providers that list HGX B300.

The pricing structure fits the RFQ. GPU pricing is per GPU-hour and covers compute, while networking and storage are provisioned separately based on your workload. ... When you request a managed cluster in the console, the form offers pay-as-you-go billing, charged by the minute with no upfront cost, and clusters are billed either pay as you go or prepaid. You also choose the data center, Kubernetes version, worker node type, node count, and OS image. The summary panel then shows the estimated monthly cost as list price, discount, and estimated total. The Managed GPU Clusters documentation walks through the form. Requests aren't processed automatically: after submitting, contact support to activate the cluster. Additional nodes on an existing cluster go through Node Requests.

results.title: Which GPU Clouds Offer Dedicated B200 Servers With Root Access and Deployment Support?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
GMI Cloud Bare Metal GPU offers dedicated B200 servers with full root access and support-led provisioning. B200 starts at $5.00 per GPU-hour on the October 2026 pricing page. Enable the organization entitlement with support, agree on SKU, IDC, and node count, and provision with registered SSH keys. CoreWeave, Together AI, and Lambda are comparison options.

...

Four providers publish NVIDIA B200 capacity on their own pages: GMI Cloud, CoreWeave, Together AI, and Lambda. The table below quotes each vendor's own page, with list prices read on October 15, 2026.

| Provider | B200 option as published | Listed price (October 2026) | How the page describes access |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GMI Cloud | "NVIDIA B200 GPU", Limited Availability | from $5.00 /GPU-hour (pricing) | "Full root access and hardware-level control"; "Dedicated physical servers for maximum performance and control" |
| CoreWeave | "NVIDIA HGX B200", 8 GPUs, 180GB VRAM per GPU | $68.80 per instance-hour, which is $8.60 per GPU-hour (pricing) | Lists Bare Metal Servers as a product alongside its Blackwell lineup |
| Together AI | "NVIDIA HGX B200 (180 GB)" | $8.19 /GPU-hour on-demand, reserved from $6.79 (GPU clusters) | "Bare-metal performance" and "Direct SSH access with Slurm simplicity" |
| Lambda | "NVIDIA HGX B200 SXM6 nodes", 1-Click Clusters from 16 to 2,000+ GPUs | $9.86 /GPU-hour at 16 GPUs on a 2-week to 1-year term (1-Click Clusters) | "Dedicated, InfiniBand-connected clusters purpose-built for AI workloads" |

The prices in that table are not quoted on the same basis. GMI Cloud prices the GPU itself and provisions the rest to fit the job: "GPU pricing covers the compute resources. Networking and storage are provisioned separately based on your workload requirements." CoreWeave's $68.80 is an instance price that includes 128 vCPUs and 2,048GB of system RAM whether the job needs that much host memory or not. Quote the GPU line and the storage and networking line together before you compare totals.

...

How much does a dedicated NVIDIA B200 server cost on GMI Cloud? The October 2026 starting rate is $5.00 per GPU-hour: $29,200 for an eight-GPU node over 730 hours. Networking and storage are separate; committed-use discounts require a quote. (GMI Cloud pricing page)

results.title: Which B200 Providers Can Plan Separate MoE Fine-Tuning and Inference Capacity?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
Pick a B200 provider that offers two different products under one account: cluster capacity you control for training, and single-tenant dedicated endpoints for serving. When each pool has its own GPU allocation and its own scheduling boundary, a training run does not compete with production traffic for the same GPUs. Separate pools also let you size, bill, and commit to each one on its own schedule. GMI Cloud covers both halves. A Managed GPU Cluster, in early access, is a Kubernetes cluster with H200 or B200 nodes, provisioned and operated by GMI, and it holds the fine-tuning pool. Prime Inference holds the inference pool: reserved single-tenant GPUs that serve your own fine-tuned or proprietary weights, loaded from Hugging Face, S3, or your own storage. On GMI Cloud, B200 is in pre-order, so today this is a reservation plan rather than capacity you can launch.

NVIDIA Blackwell on GMI Cloud, including B200, is in pre-order and coming soon, and the GPU page lists B200 pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour. What you can settle now is the plan: the shape of each pool, the handoff between them, and how the reservation is split. H100 and H200 are available now, so the two-pool workflow can be tested on H200 while the B200 reservation is arranged.

results.title: Lyceum H100 went $2.79 to $3.49, GMI $2.00 to $2.60, October 7, 2026
highlights:
On October 7, 2026, two GPU clouds we read every hour printed higher H100 rates. In our read at 19:40:43 UTC, Lyceum’s price page listed an H100 80 GB on demand at $3.49 a GPU-hour, up from $2.79 an hour earlier, a rise of 25.1%. In our read at 08:40:55 UTC, GMI Cloud’s page listed its H100 “from” $2.60 a GPU-hour, up from $2.00, a rise of 30.0%. Neither page names the form factor, so both rates sit on our H100 80GB card, where the median rate card at 06:41 UTC on October 8 was $3.51 across 20 rate cards.

...

## GMI Cloud moved three “from” rates

GMI Cloud’s pricing page prints one figure per card as “from $X /GPU-hour”, an advertised starting rate, and our tables tag it that way. In the 08:40:55 UTC read on October 7, three of its four cards moved: H100 from $2.00 to $2.60, H200 from $2.60 to $3.20 (up 23.1%) and B200 from $4.00 to $5.00 (up 25.0%). GB200 stayed at $8.00. The read at 07:40:56 UTC still printed $2.00 for the H100, and the GMI module was not changed in that window. After the move, three of the 20 H100 rate cards on October 8 listed lower than GMI’s $2.60, and eight of the 43 H200 rate cards listed lower than its $3.20.

The Price Index is computed from the H100 SXM card only. Both rates here sit on the H100 80GB card, whose pages do not name a form factor, so neither move enters the index.

...

**Ben Pouladian**: Founder, BEP Research | Covering the Co-Design Era of AI.

---

Nebius notified customers of 17–21% on-demand GPU price increases effective October 1.
For B200, the move from $7.15 to $8.50 per GPU-hour adds $1,350 per 1,000 GPU-hours, before other charges and discounts.
For compute buyers, that makes the applicable region and contract terms worth checking. For investors, a higher posted rate alone does not establish realized pricing, utilization, or margins.

## What changes in October 2026?

Nebius has published its next B200 rate: $8.50 per GPU-hour from 1 October 2026, up $1.35, or 19%, from $7.15. 8 At $8.50 it moves from fourth to fifth, behind Together AI’s $8.19 and just ahead of CoreWeave’s $8.60. Its H100 rises at the same time, from $3.85 to $4.50, so its B200-to-H100 ratio barely moves, from 1.86 to 1.89. 8 

Other pages were repriced recently. RunPod dates its pricing page 27 September 2026, and DigitalOcean’s new GPU pricing took effect on 1 August 2026. 4, 6 Together AI’s page carries a banner saying on-demand B200s are now available on its GPU Clusters. 7 This is Glamdring’s first B200 price ranking, so there’s no earlier release to compare.
